question: How do you optimize React performance? memo, useMemo, useCallback, virtualization?

scenes.sub: Skip work that would give the same answer.
scenes.say: React performance. The honest interview answer is: measure first, then skip work that would produce the same result. Four tools do that.

scenes.head: Think of a teacher
scenes.say: Think of a teacher with thirty papers. One student changes an answer. A bad teacher re-grades all thirty. A good teacher checks which paper changed, and re-grades only that one. By default React is the bad teacher: when a parent renders, every child renders too.

scenes.head: memo needs stable props
scenes.say: React dot memo wraps the list. Now, on each key you type, App re-renders, but React compares the props shallowly. Same props, so the list is skipped. The catch: a function written inline is a new function every render, so memo sees a change and re-renders anyway. Use callback keeps the same function between renders.

scenes.head: useMemo and virtualization
scenes.say: Use memo caches a computed value between renders, and recomputes only when the listed inputs change. Good for expensive filters and sorts. For huge lists the real fix is virtualization. Ten thousand rows in the D O M is slow, no matter how well you memoize. Render only the twenty or so that are visible, and swap them as the user scrolls.

scenes.head: In the interview
rows: No. Comparing props costs too. Profile first.
useMemo caches a value. memo skips a component render.
Split state down, lazy load routes, stable keys.
useCallback on a child that is not memoized. It does nothing.
scenes.say: Likely follow-ups. Should I memo everything? No, comparing props costs too. Profile first with the React profiler. Use memo versus memo? Use memo caches a value, memo skips a component render. Other quick wins? Move state down, lazy load routes, stable keys. The common mistake: use callback on a child that is not memoized. It does nothing.

lines: memo skips renders, useMemo caches values, useCallback keeps function identity.
scenes.say: Measure first with the profiler. Then memo skips renders, use memo caches values, and use callback keeps function identity stable. For huge lists, virtualize.
